items.name: riser
items.title: Riser
items.description: The outgoing page drops back into depth while the incoming page is unmasked over it. No dependencies and no JavaScript animating anything — the stylesheet drives it.
items.docs:
Wrap your layout with the transition. This is the only step:

  // app/layout.tsx
  import { RiserTransition } from "@/components/riser"

  export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
    return (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <RiserTransition direction="up">{children}</RiserTransition>
        </body>
      </html>
    )
  }

Your existing <Link>s and <a>s are intercepted automatically. New tabs,
modified clicks, downloads, external links and same-page hashes are left alone.

direction takes up, down, left or right — the incoming page is unmasked from
that edge and the outgoing page recedes the opposite way.

Needs the View Transitions API: Chrome 111+, Safari 18+, Firefox 132+. Older
browsers navigate normally with no animation.

items.name: film-burn
items.title: Film Burn
items.description: The page catches alight and the fire burns straight through it to the page underneath. One continuous burn, no dependencies — it rides the browser's View Transitions API.
items.docs:
Wrap your layout with the transition. This is the only step:

  // app/layout.tsx
  import { FilmBurnTransition } from "@/components/film-burn"

  export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
    return (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <FilmBurnTransition>{children}</FilmBurnTransition>
        </body>
      </html>
    )
  }

Your existing <Link>s and <a>s are intercepted automatically. New tabs,
modified clicks, downloads, external links and same-page hashes are left alone.

The fire starts from a random corner each navigation. Pass origin="top-left"
(or top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right, center) to fix it.

Colour: four presets ship as classes — palette="ember" (default), "magnesium",
"cold" or "toxic". For anything else pass palette="custom" and set
--burn-core, --burn-hot, --burn-mid and --burn-edge yourself.

Needs the View Transitions API: Chrome 111+, Safari 18+, Firefox 132+. Older
browsers navigate normally with no animation — nothing breaks, but there is no
fallback effect.

items.name: zipper
items.title: Zipper
items.description: A zip runs down the screen, catching twice before it runs, seals the page behind it, then the two halves fall open sideways. GSAP.
items.docs:
Wrap your layout with the transition. This is the only step:

  // app/layout.tsx
  import { ZipperTransition } from "@/components/zipper"

  export default function RootLayout({ children }) {
    return (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <ZipperTransition>{children}</ZipperTransition>
        </body>
      </html>
    )
  }

Your existing <Link>s are intercepted automatically.

Colour: five presets ship as classes — put zip-steel, zip-brass, zip-gunmetal
or zip-copper on any ancestor of the transition. For anything else, set
--zip-metal-hi/-metal/-mid/-lo/-edge and --zip-tape/-lo yourself in
components/transitions.css.

Note: browser back/forward is not animated, and the route does not start
loading until the leave phase finishes (~1.5s).

items.name: crayon
items.title: Crayon Wipe
items.description: Three hand-drawn strokes draw across the screen, the route swaps behind them, then they retract away. GSAP.
